_comment: Every public claim on monogate.dev that a Lean theorem is proved, pinned to the artifact that proves it. `npm run check:site` runs ../monogate-lean/tools/lean_claims/check_claims.py over it on every deploy: each claimed theorem must be declared in its file at the pinned revision, the file must compile in its environment (toolchain and every package revision below exactly as pinned; imports only from Lean core, those packages, and the local source trees pinned under `sources`, whose build must be current), each theorem's own #print axioms must have no sorryAx and nothing outside allowed_axioms, and every label occurrence in the scanned paths must be a site below or an exemption with its reason. A site may sit outside the scanned paths, as the Electronics Lab bundle in public/ does; it must still appear in its file. To make a new claim, add it here in the same change. After `lake update` in an environment, re-pin its packages here. To move to a newer machlib, move the `sources` pin and every claim's `revision` together.

claims.statement: the cost theory's named results on /superbest, badged machine-checked; the page promises only propext and Quot.sound

The Electronics Lab labels the theorem behind its FPGA arccos certificate "sorryAx-free, lake build clean". That label lives only in the vendored bundle: public/electronics-lab is a Vite build synced by scripts/sync_electronics_lab_public.py from the private monogate-electronics repo, whose build_evidence_packet.py types the string and never runs lake. Editing the bundle here would break SOURCE.json's sha256 manifest and be undone by the next sync, so the label is gated instead: the theorem must compile at the pinned machlib with no sorryAx. A re-sync renames the hashed bundle file, which fails this site as STALE_SITE until it is re-pinned.
As electronics-acos-forward-error, for the FPGA arcsin certificate.
As electronics-acos-forward-error, for the FPGA sine certificate; the bundle also cites this theorem, labelled "sorryAx-free", for a simulation-and-build packet with no theorem_file.
As electronics-acos-forward-error, for the FPGA tangent certificate.
As electronics-acos-forward-error, for the FPGA tanh certificate.

The Electronics Lab's Reflex contract lab says #print axioms ran against the built MachLib and shows "sorryAx-free" for MachLib.Real.fx_sound. Same vendored-bundle situation as electronics-acos-forward-error.

exempt.reason: a COUNT of MachLib theorems, not a claim about one: the figure beside it is checked against machlib's README by check_site_figures.mjs, and machlib's own prose gate ties that README row to tools/count_theorems.py
a course description (the Foundations track teaches up to machine-checked certificates); it asserts no theorem is proved
